summary: CI: private upgrade E2E jobs timing out (N-1 → N) in nightly + some PR gating runs
description:
Issue summary
- Multiple private upgrade end-to-end CI jobs are exceeding configured job time limits (90m) and being killed, primarily in the nightly suite but also intermittently in PR gating for upgrade-related changes.
- Failures are clustered around upgrade apply / post-upgrade verification stages where we wait for Helm hook jobs (migrations, preupgrade checks) and for data-plane rollouts.

Impact
- Nightly signal for “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” is degraded (false negatives). PRs touching installer/charts are delayed due to re-runs and manual triage.
- Risk: release gating for Private upgrades becomes unreliable, increasing chance of regressions landing without coverage.

What’s failing (examples)
- Job: private-upgrade-e2e (k8s 1.28, CSI/Rook) 
  - Step that times out: “installer upgrade apply”
  - Last log line (typical):
    - "Waiting for job/redwood-migrate to complete (hook: pre-upgrade)"
    - "helm upgrade --install … timed out waiting for the condition"
- Job: private-upgrade-e2e (k8s 1.27, EBS) 
  - Step that times out: “post-upgrade verify”
  - Last log line (typical):
    - "Waiting for deployment/redwood-control-plane to become Ready"

Scope / test context
- Suite executes N-1 → N in-place upgrade for Redwood Private on ephemeral clusters.
- Currently includes control-plane first, then data-plane, plus verification (API health, DB connectivity, basic inference smoke).

Investigation notes
1) Pattern analysis (last 10 occurrences)
- ~60%: stuck in Helm hook job completion (migrate/preupgrade) until job timeout.
- ~30%: image pull delays on cold runners (large images + no local cache). Logs show extended time between “Pulling image …” and container start; also occasional registry throttling on the runner egress path.
- ~10%: slow rollout for data-plane deployment due to node resource pressure; observed pending pods waiting on CPU/memory on smaller runner nodes.

2) Cluster signals (from job artifacts)
- kubectl get jobs shows migrate job in Active for >45m in several failures.
- migrate logs sometimes show long lock waits / low output frequency, which makes it hard to tell if it’s making progress or deadlocked.
- When we repro locally with debug, migration itself completes but total wall time varies heavily depending on image pull cache state.

3) Recent changes that could contribute
- Chart hook ordering / timeouts were adjusted recently; this may have increased the time we wait for hooks by default in some scenarios.
- DB migration guardrails are landing (idempotency + lock timeouts), but not fully rolled into the E2E suite baseline at the time of the earliest failures.

Root cause (most likely)
- CI wall-clock time variance pushed the suite over the global job timeout:
  - cold runner image pulls + no pre-pull caching
  - helm hook jobs have conservative timeouts and can sit waiting on DB locks with limited progress output
  - cluster sizing for some E2E permutations is near the minimum, causing rollout delays

Mitigation / changes applied
Immediate (done)
- Increased CI job timeout from 90m → 150m for private-upgrade-e2e nightly jobs while we stabilize (temporary).
- Reduced concurrency for the heaviest permutations to avoid saturating runner node resources.
- Added artifact collection on timeout (kubectl describe jobs/pods, events, top nodes) to make future failures actionable.

Short-term (done / in progress)
- Added an explicit pre-pull step for the heaviest images used in the suite on self-hosted runners.
- Adjusted helm upgrade invocation in the E2E harness to emit periodic progress (polling rollout status with timestamps) so “stalls” are visible.

Follow-ups (tracked outside this ticket)
- Split the suite: separate “upgrade apply” from “post-upgrade verify” so a single slow rollout doesn’t consume the whole budget.
- Improve determinism: pin base images and preload images into runner cache for nightly.
- Ensure DB migration jobs have bounded lock wait + clear failure mode; align E2E baseline with migration guardrails.

Acceptance criteria
- Nightly private-upgrade-e2e suite passes 5 consecutive runs without timeout.
- If timeouts occur, artifacts must identify the bottleneck stage (image pull vs hook job vs rollout) within 5 minutes of triage.

Resolution
- After applying timeout bump + runner pre-pull + improved artifact capture, the last 6 nightly runs (2025-06-09 through 2025-06-11) completed within 78–112 minutes and did not hit the global timeout.
- Marking as Resolved; keeping watch via nightly dashboard and will reopen if timeouts recur.
comments: 2025-06-06 09:18 (Sahana Iyer): Creating INT for repeated private upgrade E2E timeouts. Seen 3/5 nightlies fail this week; also hit once on PR gating for charts. Attaching last job logs + timestamps in build artifacts.

2025-06-06 10:02 (Devon Price): Taking. First look: global 90m job timeout triggers before helm upgrade timeout in a few cases. Suspect image pull + small runner nodes. Will add artifact capture on cancel and compare wall time distribution.

2025-06-07 14:41 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on resource pressure. In two failures, nodes were ~95% mem; data-plane pods pending for ~20m. Recommend reducing concurrency or bump runner size for the heavy permutations.

2025-06-08 11:27 (Devon Price): Implemented timeout bump to 150m for nightly only + reduced concurrency for the Rook/CSI permutation. Also added on-timeout collection of kubectl get/describe + events. Next nightly should be more actionable.

2025-06-09 08:05 (Devon Price): Nightly passed (total 101m). Biggest single chunk was image pull (~23m) on cold runner. Adding explicit pre-pull step for images referenced by installer + charts to cut variance.

2025-06-10 16:12 (Sahana Iyer): PR gating still on 90m and is borderline for the heaviest matrix. Suggest we either (a) split the test or (b) run only a lighter permutation on PR gating and keep full matrix nightly.
2025-06-11 09:36 (Devon Price): Last 6 nightlies green (78–112m). Pre-pull reduced worst-case pull time. Marking resolved with plan to split suite for PR gating in follow-up work.
